However, the BF gas is available for this project at low pressure of 16.7 psia, and the conditioned gas after the WGS island needs to be at low pressure for the carbon capture process. Thus, appropriate system engineering has been carried out by Dastur to ensure the following: a) The conditioned gas after the WGS island attains a pressure of 16.7 psia. b) Reactors are designed to work with minimum operating pressure and minimum pressure drop. c) The pressure drop across the WGS island is minimum, and thus, the compressor power requirement is minimum. d) The gas attains an S: DG ratio of 0.57 before entering the WGS reactor e) Appropriate heat integration after the WGS reactor to generate quality steam for the project and cool the conditioned gas to 91oF. The BF gas compressor and NG-fired pre-heater have been considered to pre-heat the BF gas at 767oF and attain the pressure of 44 psia before entering to WGS reactor, considering the total pressure drop across the WGS island. A steam mixing arrangement is considered before the WGS reactor. Since the shift reaction is exothermic, BG gas attains a higher temperature of 839oF before leaving the WGS reactor. To cool the hot gas coming out of the WGS reactor from 839oF to 91oF with minimum pressure drop, Dastur has designed: a) WGS boiler to generate adequate steam for WGS process requirement, b) Boiler feed water pre-heater to preheat water and further heat recovery c) Quench tower to reduce gas stream temperature with minimum water requirement with lower capex and pressure drop. Thus, the entire WGS island is designed to ensure operation at low-pressure.
